newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo questions Zaire rebels on mine tender.
newsitem.headline: Anglo questions Zaire rebels on mine tender.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, denied a lucrative Zairean mining project by Laurent Kabila's rebels, said on Friday the tender process for the project had not been allowed to run its full course.
The South African mining giant tendered to develop the Kolwezi copper/cobalt talings project along with a number of international mining companies.
But Kabila's AFDL earlier this month awarded the contract to U.S-based America Mineral Fields Inc.

Anglo said on Friday it had held discussions -- focussing on a number of business issues relating to tenders submitted to Zaire's state-owned mining company Gecamines (Generale des Carriers et des Mines) -- with the rebels in Lubumbashi this week.

"In particular, the corporation sought clarification on the recent decision by the (AFDL) alliance to award the Kolwezi Tailings Project, apparently ahead of formal completion of the tender adjudication process by Gecamines," Anglo said in a statement.
It said its bid for Kolwezi was above board and conducted "directly and properly" with Gecamines management.
"Regrettably, Anglo American Corporation has concluded that the tendering process for the Kolwezi Tailings Project has not been allowed to run its full course," Anglo said.
Kabila's rebels awarded the project to AMF in a $1 billion deal which also included the planned construction of a 200,000 tonne/year zinc smelter at Kipushi.
Anglo spokeswoman Charmane Russell said there was very little the corporation could do now about the way the tender had been awarded and that legal action was unlikely.
"There is very little we can do. They (the rebels) have noted our concerns," she said. No further discussions were planned with Kabila's rebels.
Anglo had submitted another tender to develop another copper/cobalt project at Ruashi-Etoile, near Lubumbashi.

Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's embattled government said last week that it was annulling all contracts between Gecamines and AMF because AMF had "violated the regulations governing the signing of mining contracts and conventions".
Waging a rebellion against Mobutu's government for six months now, Kabila's AFDL is in control of more than half of Zaire including all mineral-producing areas.
An agreement between AMF and Anglo to jointly develop the Kolwezi project, was cancelled earlier this year.
